glossary.definition: A legal member of a country who has rights, duties, and responsibilities.
glossary.example: A Ghanaian citizen has the right to vote and the duty to obey the laws of Ghana.

glossary.definition: The status of being a member of a country with rights and responsibilities.
glossary.example: Citizenship can be acquired by birth, registration, or naturalization.

glossary.definition: The process by which a foreigner legally becomes a citizen of a country.
glossary.example: A person from another country who lives in Ghana for years can apply for citizenship through naturalization.

glossary.definition: The country to which a person legally belongs.
glossary.example: Your nationality tells which country you are a citizen of, such as Ghanaian.

glossary.definition: A system of government in which the people have the power, usually through free elections.
glossary.example: In Ghana citizens vote to choose their leaders.

glossary.definition: The group of people who make decisions and run the affairs of a country.
glossary.example: The government of Ghana makes laws and provides schools and roads.

glossary.definition: The written set of laws that explains how a country should be governed.
glossary.example: Ghana's 1992 Constitution is the highest law of the country.

glossary.definition: The Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary which keep power balanced.
glossary.example: Parliament makes laws, the President carries them out, courts interpret them.

glossary.definition: The arm of government that makes the laws of the country.
glossary.example: In Ghana Parliament is the legislature.

glossary.definition: The arm of government that carries out or enforces the laws.
glossary.example: The President and ministers are part of the Executive.

glossary.definition: The arm of government that interprets the laws in the courts.
glossary.example: The Supreme Court is the head of the Judiciary in Ghana.

glossary.definition: The process by which citizens vote to choose their leaders.
glossary.example: Ghana holds national elections every four years.

glossary.definition: The right to vote in elections.
glossary.example: In Ghana suffrage is granted to every citizen aged 18 and above.

glossary.definition: The principle that everyone including leaders must obey the law.
glossary.example: The rule of law means no one is above the law.

glossary.definition: The basic freedoms that belong to every person at birth.
glossary.example: The right to life, education, and freedom of speech are human rights.

glossary.definition: Rights are what you are entitled to; responsibilities are your duties.
glossary.example: You have the right to education and the responsibility to attend school.

glossary.definition: Being responsible for your actions and willing to answer for them.
glossary.example: A minister is accountable to Parliament for public money.

glossary.definition: Everything around us that affects living things.
glossary.example: The environment includes air, water, soil, plants, and animals.

glossary.definition: The condition of the atmosphere over a short period.
glossary.example: Today it is sunny and hot.

glossary.definition: The average weather condition of a place over many years.
glossary.example: Ghana's southern region has a tropical climate with high rainfall.

glossary.definition: The breaking down of rocks into smaller pieces by natural forces.
glossary.example: Rain and wind slowly break down a large rock into sand.

glossary.definition: The moving away of soil or rock particles by water, wind, or ice.
glossary.example: Heavy rain washes away topsoil from a farm.

glossary.definition: Things found in nature that people use to satisfy their needs.
glossary.example: Gold, timber, water, and fish are natural resources of Ghana.

glossary.definition: A natural resource that can be replaced or regrown over time.
glossary.example: Trees and water are renewable resources.

glossary.definition: A natural resource that cannot easily be replaced once used up.
glossary.example: Gold and oil are non-renewable resources.

glossary.definition: The cutting down and removal of trees from a forest area.
glossary.example: Deforestation leads to soil erosion and loss of animal habitats.

glossary.definition: The making of the environment dirty or harmful by waste or poison.
glossary.example: Burning rubbish produces air pollution.

glossary.definition: Illegal small-scale gold mining that damages the environment.
glossary.example: Galamsey pollutes rivers and destroys farmlands.

glossary.definition: The careful use and protection of natural resources so they last.
glossary.example: Planting trees is a way to practice conservation.

glossary.definition: The total number of people living in a place or country.
glossary.example: Ghana's population is over 30 million.

glossary.definition: The number of births for every 1,000 people in a year.
glossary.example: A high birth rate means many babies are born each year.

glossary.definition: The number of deaths for every 1,000 people in a year.
glossary.example: A low death rate means people receive good health care.

glossary.definition: Relating to the countryside with few people and fewer services.
glossary.example: Villages in northern Ghana are rural areas.

glossary.definition: Relating to a city or town with many people and services.
glossary.example: Accra and Kumasi are urban areas.

glossary.definition: The movement of people from the countryside to the cities.
glossary.example: Many young people move from villages to Accra for jobs.

glossary.definition: Farming and the raising of crops and animals for food.
glossary.example: Ghana grows cocoa, maize, and yams through agriculture.

glossary.definition: The buying and selling of goods and services.
glossary.example: Ghana exports cocoa and imports machinery through trade.

glossary.definition: Goods brought into a country from abroad.
glossary.example: Petrol and machinery are imports of Ghana.

glossary.definition: Goods sent out of a country to be sold abroad.
glossary.example: Cocoa is a major export of Ghana.

glossary.definition: A plan showing how money will be earned and spent over a period.
glossary.example: The government presents a national budget each year.

glossary.definition: Money people and businesses pay to the government for public services.
glossary.example: The government uses taxes to build roads and schools.

glossary.definition: The state of people who are willing to work but cannot find jobs.
glossary.example: Unemployment is high among young school leavers.

glossary.definition: The way of life of a people including language, food, clothing, and beliefs.
glossary.example: Kente cloth and fufu are parts of Ghanaian culture.

glossary.definition: A belief or custom passed down from one generation to the next.
glossary.example: Performing Homowo festival every year is a tradition of the Ga people.

glossary.definition: A special time of celebration where people remember an event or give thanks.
glossary.example: Homowo, Odwira, and Aboakyer are festivals in Ghana.

glossary.definition: The state of being free from the control of another country.
glossary.example: Ghana gained independence from Britain on 6 March 1957.

glossary.definition: The controlling of one country by another to take its resources.
glossary.example: Ghana was under British colonialism until 1957.

glossary.definition: A movement that unites African people and countries across the world.
glossary.example: Kwame Nkrumah promoted Pan-Africanism and African unity.

glossary.definition: The family relationship between people based on blood or marriage.
glossary.example: Kinship ties in Ghana guide who can marry whom.

glossary.definition: The illegal moving and trading of people to force them to work.
glossary.example: Human trafficking is a serious crime that violates human rights.

glossary.definition: The responsibilities that every citizen must perform for the good of the country.
glossary.example: Paying taxes and voting are civic duties.

glossary.definition: A system where leaders are chosen by the people and power is shared.
glossary.example: Ghana practices democratic governance through periodic elections.

glossary.definition: The right to vote given to eligible citizens.
glossary.example: The franchise was extended to all adults in Ghana in 1992.

glossary.definition: Organizations that put forward candidates to contest elections and form government.
glossary.example: NPP and NDC are the two main political parties in Ghana.

glossary.definition: The transfer of power from the central government to local authorities.
glossary.example: District assemblies are part of Ghana's decentralization policy.

glossary.definition: Government at the district, municipal, or city level that serves local needs.
glossary.example: The district assembly provides water and sanitation in the area.

glossary.definition: A direct vote by all eligible citizens on a particular proposal or law.
glossary.example: Ghana held a referendum to approve the 1992 Constitution.

glossary.definition: The current supreme law of Ghana that established multi-party democracy.
glossary.example: The 1992 Constitution allows multiple political parties and elections.

glossary.definition: The shape and height of the land surface of an area.
glossary.example: Ghana has low-lying coastal plains and hilly areas in the north.

glossary.definition: Areas with similar types of plant life determined by climate.
glossary.example: Ghana has three main vegetation zones: coastal, forest, and savanna.

glossary.definition: A grassland area with scattered trees and distinct wet and dry seasons.
glossary.example: The northern part of Ghana is mostly savanna.

glossary.definition: A dense forest in tropical areas with heavy rainfall all year.
glossary.example: The Ashanti and Western regions of Ghana have tropical rainforest.

glossary.definition: Valuable substances found in the earth such as gold, diamonds, and bauxite.
glossary.example: Ghana is rich in mineral resources like gold and bauxite.

glossary.definition: Sources of water that people use such as rivers, lakes, and underground water.
glossary.example: The Volta River is one of Ghana's major water resources.

glossary.definition: The gradual increase in the earth's temperature caused by greenhouse gases.
glossary.example: Global warming is caused by deforestation and burning fossil fuels.

glossary.definition: The process by which fertile land becomes desert due to drought or poor farming.
glossary.example: Overgrazing and deforestation can lead to desertification in northern Ghana.

glossary.definition: The thinning of the ozone layer caused by harmful chemicals.
glossary.example: CFCs from old refrigerators cause ozone depletion.

glossary.definition: An overflow of water that covers land that is usually dry.
glossary.example: Heavy rains cause flooding in Accra every rainy season.

glossary.definition: A long period with little or no rainfall, causing water shortage.
glossary.example: Drought in northern Ghana makes it hard to grow crops.

glossary.definition: The proper collection, treatment, and disposal of waste.
glossary.example: Recycling and composting are forms of waste management.

glossary.definition: Rain made acidic by air pollution that damages buildings and plants.
glossary.example: Acid rain damages forests and corrodes metal structures.

glossary.definition: Excessive or harmful noise that affects the health of people and animals.
glossary.example: Loud music from clubs at night is a form of noise pollution.

glossary.definition: An official count of the population of a country at a particular time.
glossary.example: Ghana conducts a population census every ten years.

glossary.definition: The process by which more people move to and live in cities.
glossary.example: Urbanization in Ghana is increasing as people move to Accra and Kumasi.

glossary.definition: When a place has too many people for the resources available.
glossary.example: Overcrowding in cities can lead to overpopulation.

glossary.definition: The money used in a particular country.
glossary.example: The currency of Ghana is the Cedi.

glossary.definition: The business of providing services for people visiting a place for pleasure.
glossary.example: Tourism in Ghana includes visits to castles and national parks.

glossary.definition: The process of making products from raw materials using machines.
glossary.example: Ghana manufactures cocoa products, textiles, and cement.

glossary.definition: Gross Domestic Product - the total value of goods and services produced in a country in a year.
glossary.example: Ghana's GDP grows when the economy produces more goods and services.

glossary.definition: The process of learning and acquiring knowledge and skills.
glossary.example: Education is a right for every child in Ghana.

glossary.definition: The state of being free from illness or injury.
glossary.example: Good health allows people to work and learn effectively.

glossary.definition: The state of being extremely poor and lacking basic needs.
glossary.example: Poverty means not having enough food, shelter, or healthcare.

glossary.definition: The use of children in work that deprives them of education and childhood.
glossary.example: Child labour is illegal in Ghana and must be stopped.

glossary.definition: Equal rights and opportunities for men and women.
glossary.example: Gender equality means girls and boys have the same chance to go to school.

glossary.definition: Health services and measures provided by the government for the whole community.
glossary.example: Vaccination programmes are part of public health.

glossary.definition: Conditions relating to public health especially through clean water and waste disposal.
glossary.example: Good sanitation prevents diseases like cholera.

glossary.definition: The first President of Ghana who led the country to independence in 1957.
glossary.example: Nkrumah declared Ghana's independence on 6 March 1957.

glossary.definition: The former name of Ghana when it was a British colony.
glossary.example: Ghana was known as the Gold Coast before independence.

glossary.definition: Six Ghanaian leaders who were jailed by the British for fighting for independence.
glossary.example: The Big Six included Kwame Nkrumah and J.B. Danquah.

glossary.definition: The sudden overthrow of a government by a small group, often the military.
glossary.example: Ghana experienced several coups before the current democratic era.

glossary.definition: A country governed by elected representatives and a president, not a king.
glossary.example: Ghana became a republic in 1960 with Nkrumah as president.

glossary.definition: The date Ghana gained independence from British colonial rule.
glossary.example: Every 6 March is celebrated as Ghana's Independence Day.

glossary.definition: The traditional practices and accepted behaviours of a group of people.
glossary.example: It is a custom in Ghana to greet elders before speaking to them.

glossary.definition: Ceremonies that mark important stages in a person's life such as birth, adulthood, and marriage.
glossary.example: Outdooring is a Ghanaian rite of passage for newborn babies.

glossary.definition: A group of families that share a common ancestor and identity.
glossary.example: In Ghana clans determine marriage rules and social relationships.

glossary.definition: Traditional leaders in Ghanaian communities who govern and maintain culture.
glossary.example: The chief settles disputes and the queen mother advises on community matters.

glossary.definition: A powerful pre-colonial kingdom in central Ghana known for its gold and culture.
glossary.example: The Ashanti Kingdom had its capital at Kumasi and was famous for Kente cloth.

glossary.definition: The largest ethnic group in Ghana, including the Ashanti and Fante.
glossary.example: The Akan people speak Twi and Fante languages.

glossary.definition: A flag that represents a country and its identity.
glossary.example: The Ghana flag has red, gold, and green stripes with a black star.

glossary.definition: A patriotic song adopted as the official song of a country.
glossary.example: The Ghana national anthem is called God Bless Our Homeland Ghana.

questions.question: The thinning of the ___ layer allows harmful UV rays through.
questions.explanation: The ozone layer protects from UV radiation.

questions.question: Global warming is caused by deforestation and fossil fuels.
questions.explanation: These activities release greenhouse gases.

questions.question: Rain made harmful by air pollution is called ___ rain.
questions.explanation: Acid rain damages buildings and forests.

questions.question: Six leaders jailed for fighting independence: The Big ___.
questions.explanation: The Big Six were jailed for demanding independence.

questions.question: Which is an example of manufacturing?
questions.explanation: Manufacturing turns raw materials into products.

questions.question: Ghana's GDP grows when the economy...
questions.explanation: GDP grows with increased production.

questions.question: Equal rights for men and women is called gender ___.
questions.explanation: Gender equality means fairness for all genders.

questions.question: The growth of cities as people move to them is called ___.
questions.explanation: Urbanization is increasing movement to cities.

questions.question: Too many people for available resources is called ___.
questions.explanation: Overpopulation strains resources.

questions.question: Nkrumah declared independence at which location?
questions.explanation: Nkrumah declared at the Old Polo Grounds.

questions.question: The powerful pre-colonial kingdom in central Ghana was the ___ Kingdom.
questions.explanation: The Ashanti Kingdom was a major pre-colonial state.

questions.question: Ghana first became a republic in 1960 under Nkrumah.
questions.explanation: Ghana became a republic on 1 July 1960.

questions.question: Ceremonies marking life stages are called rites of ___.
questions.explanation: Rites of passage mark key life transitions.

questions.question: The Gold Coast was the former name of...
questions.explanation: Ghana was called the Gold Coast during colonialism.

questions.question: Acid rain is caused by harmful gases mixing with rainwater.
questions.explanation: Pollutant gases dissolve in rain to form acid rain.

questions.question: A cause of drought in northern Ghana is...
questions.explanation: Poor land use contributes to drought.

questions.question: A consequence of rural-urban migration is...
questions.explanation: Migration to cities causes overcrowding.

questions.question: Which is a social development indicator?
questions.explanation: Education access shows social development.

questions.question: The movement uniting African people is called Pan-___.
questions.explanation: Pan-Africanism promotes African unity.

questions.question: The 1992 Constitution established which system?
questions.explanation: The 1992 Constitution established multi-party democracy.

questions.question: The queen mother advises on community matters in traditional governance.
questions.explanation: The queen mother plays an advisory role.

questions.question: Greeting elders before speaking is an example of...
questions.explanation: This is a traditional custom in Ghana.

questions.question: Clean water and proper waste disposal is called ___.
questions.explanation: Good sanitation prevents disease.

questions.question: In Ghana clans determine...
questions.explanation: Clans guide marriage and social relationships.

questions.question: The Ghana national anthem is also known as...
questions.explanation: This is the official national anthem.

questions.question: The largest subgroup of the Akan people is the...
questions.explanation: The Ashanti are the largest Akan subgroup.
